component.title: The sequent kernel: the polarized L command IL, machine, and fusion engine (phases L0-L2)

section.title: Overview and decisions
section.prose:
The sequent kernel adopts a polarized command IL — a System-L (lambda-mu-mu-tilde) intermediate language whose producers, consumers, and commands are first-class, arena-resident, inspectable IR — as gandr's machine-and-optimization IL, beside the frozen call-by-push-value core
, which remains the source and typing calculus. A static focusing translation bridges them. The correspondence is established: polarized L is call-by-push-value in sequent form
, and the machine gandr already had is sequent-shaped, so the kernel reifies existing structure rather than replacing it
.

This component absorbs the three additive phases the kernel work builds on. Phase L0 reifies the command IL and the focusing translation; phase L1 runs the focused IL on the L machine — the iterative, first-order, arena-native driver — over a two-region store, executing the full effect and control surface; phase L2 is a fusion engine over command seams, the reserved rule 2-cells completed into a convergent system whose derived cells carry replayable certificates. Phase L3, named but not decided, is an explicit, evidence-gated promotion decision. No phase touches the frozen core before L3. A deferred glued-NbE re-sequencing rides the same machine.

The reboot carries L0 as built and L1 as partial (crate core-sequent) and the L2 fusion engine as built (crate theory-computads), beside the frozen core and touching no frozen-core code: the kernel consumes the public core-checker surface, and the fusion engine consumes the public command-IL vocabulary, read-only. The later closures lane and glued NbE are absorbed here as design records, not yet shipped code.

section.title: The kernel IL
section.prose: Three syntactic categories. A producer p introduces values and captures contexts; a consumer c is a covariable, a binder, a destructor frame, a pattern match, or the terminal consumer; a command s is a cut carrying a polarity, a native operation, or a top-level jump. Every node is arena-resident and binders close over environments, never host closures.

grammar.production: x | lit | μα. s | K(p̄; c̄) | cocase { D(x̄; ᾱ) ⇒ s, … }
α | μ̃x. s | D(p̄; c̄) | case { K(x̄; ᾱ) ⇒ s, … } | ★

section.prose: A cut ⟨p |ε c⟩ is the machine's redex site: it carries a polarity ε and requires the producer and consumer to meet at the same type, with ε matching that type's polarity. Mixed argument lists are semicolon-separated (producers before consumers); a destructor's trailing consumer is its return continuation, so a stack frame is a covalue. The IL's own discipline is the two-sided sequent (internal to core-sequent, a debug-assertion face used by the differential harness, not the user-facing gate):

section.title: Focusing: the core-to-command translation
section.prose: Surface elaboration continues to target the frozen core. A static focusing translation takes checked core computations to focused commands; it is the only entry into the IL, so the machine only ever sees focused states (progress holds only for focused commands — un-focused input can be stuck). Focusing is administrative-redex-avoiding and total on well-formed core terms — a phase-L0 gate — and is itself differentially anchored (a checked term and its focused image denote the same observable outcome).
section.code: 𝓕⟦ret v⟧ α = ⟨𝓥⟦v⟧ | α⟩ 𝓕⟦let x ← t; u⟧ α = 𝓕⟦t⟧ (μ̃x. 𝓕⟦u⟧ α) -- Bind is μ̃ 𝓕⟦t v⟧ α = 𝓕⟦t⟧ (ap(𝓥⟦v⟧; α)) -- application is the ap destructor 𝓕⟦λx. t⟧ = cocase { ap(x; α) ⇒ 𝓕⟦t⟧ α } -- the IL-internal function representation 𝓕⟦force v⟧ α = ⟨𝓥⟦v⟧ | force(α)⟩ -- the U-shift destructor 𝓕⟦case v {…}⟧ α = ⟨𝓥⟦v⟧ | case { K(x̄) ⇒ 𝓕⟦tᵢ⟧ α, … }⟩
section.prose: Two spec-anchored correspondences the reboot pins: a stack frame is a consumer (the argument coterm is ap, the bind continuation is μ̃, a projection is a destructor), and a lambda or lazy pair is a cocase (negative introduction eliminated by copatterns). Two classical wins arrive free: case-of-case (commuting conversions are plain μ-reductions, no pass) and label/goto as derived forms (μ is lexically-scoped context capture).

section.title: The L machine and its store
section.prose: The L machine is a flat loop over the cut cases — iterative by construction, serializable and inspectable at every step (commands, consumers, and the store are all IR data). Each transition extends the environment; none substitutes textually. A terminal state is ⟨𝔭 | ★⟩.
section.code: ⟨μα.s |ε c⟩ ↦ s with env[α ↦ eval_c(c)] (fires first when ε = +) ⟨𝔭 |ε μ̃x.s⟩ ↦ s with env[x ↦ eval_p(𝔭)] (fires first when ε = −) ⟨K(𝔭̄;𝔠̄) | case {…, K(x̄;ᾱ) ⇒ s, …}⟩ ↦ s with env[x̄↦𝔭̄, ᾱ↦𝔠̄] ⟨cocase {…, D(x̄;ᾱ) ⇒ s, …} | D(𝔭̄;𝔠̄)⟩ ↦ s with env[x̄↦𝔭̄, ᾱ↦𝔠̄] prim(𝔭̄; c̄) ↦ dispatch to the native registry, feeding results to c̄ f(𝔭̄; c̄) ↦ the body of f with env[params] (a jump; no call stack)
section.prose:
The two-region store pairs a persistent heap for duplicable values with a frame stack of addressable equation frames, under a shrink rule (returning through a covalue drops every frame allocated after it)
. The store keeps the machine's own call-by-need semantics — a memo cell (unforced, in-progress, forced, with black-holing) is a stored negative binding with update-on-force. Residency is a per-cell store property, never a type former: grades inform initial placement (a heuristic) while an escape-promotion barrier carries soundness. L1 ships heap-everything behind a region-shaped API, so the machine differential measures the machine and not placement; the refined grade-to-region map is a gated follow-on.

section.title: Glued NbE re-sequenced onto the L machine
section.prose:
Glued normalization-by-evaluation — the two-mechanism split of a syntactic face beside a semantic face — is re-sequenced onto the
rather than the retired CEK oracle it was first framed against. The
is the glue table: the syntactic face is the arena node graph, the semantic face is the forced-cell layer. Conversion checking, when it arrives with the levitation-stage-1 descriptions and the sized-types discipline of the negative surface, quotients size annotations under size-irrelevance. Building gluing once, on the machine that will keep it, avoids a CEK retrofit the L machine would immediately obsolete; the design takes the polarized-call-by-push-value NbE line as its reference
. It is deferred, not built: no NbE face exists in the reboot yet, and the item stays queued behind the machine and the levitation-stage-1 landing.

section.title: Strategy as polarity orientation
section.prose: The command ⟨μα.s₁ | μ̃x.s₂⟩ is the fundamental critical pair: μ wants to capture the consumer, μ̃ wants to bind the producer, and the two results differ. The resolution is typed and local — polarity orientation : every cut carries ε, positive cuts give μ priority (call-by-value, data flows), negative cuts give μ̃ priority (call-by-name, demand flows). The type fixes ε, so determinism is restored per seam rather than by a global language switch, and an evaluation strategy becomes an orientation choice on a cell. Two consequences bind the engine: η-laws are strategy-tied (codata η only under call-by-name, data η only under call-by-value), and ε is always derivable from the type at elaboration, so the IL never guesses.

section.title: Effects and control as consumer patterns
section.prose: The three existing control mechanisms translate into one shape — case analysis on the consumer side. A deep handler is a consumer case on operation constructors binding the resumption as a covalue; reset is a prompt covalue; shift captures the consumer up to it (μ-capture); break and continue are effect operations caught by loop handlers. Deep handlers re-install themselves in the captured resumption exactly as before, and the captured slice is first-class IL data rather than a name-keyed side table — strictly more inspectable.
section.code: handler H = handler { opᵢ(x̄; k) ⇒ sᵢ, …, return(x) ⇒ s₀ } (a consumer) perform ⟨op(𝔭̄) | H⟩ ↦ sᵢ with x̄ ↦ 𝔭̄, k ↦ the delimited resumption covalue reset = a prompt covalue; shift captures the consumer up to it (μ-capture)
section.prose:
The posture is translate, don't redesign: the surface (perform, handle, reset, shift, and the loop operations) is unchanged; only the machine realization becomes consumer-shaped. The
is unchanged by this translation. It is a
: the L machine must present the identical host seam the earlier machine did, over the public value and effect-signature surface, so the headless host-effect runtime binds against the same contract regardless of which machine drives it.

section.title: Fusion by completion (phase L2)
section.prose:
Program transformation is ordinary rewriting in the IL, with certificates. The kernel's optimization layer is fusion by completion : the reserved rule 2-cells of a data block — the surface
faces — elaborate to command rewrites; overlaps where two rewrites meet at a cut are bona-fide critical pairs; and a completion engine synthesizes derived, fused cells carrying replayable certificates, differential-tested against the two-step composite. There are no rewrite pragmas — the anti-pragma posture of the polygraph program (decision K5). This is completion over the convergent slice of a
, and it is the optimization-time twin of the runtime
stance. It is engineered in crate theory-computads, the third purely-additive phase of the kernel: it consumes the public command-IL vocabulary read-only and touches no frozen-core code.

section.title: What a rule becomes
section.prose: A data block reserves op and rule productions (the anti-retrofit guard of the data surface); their elaboration target is the cell store. An operation op f(…) reifies as an operation frame family f(remaining-args; return-consumer) — an f-application waiting at the seam — and a rule (an oriented left-to-right arrow) elaborates to an oriented command cell whose left side is a cut between a constructor pattern and an operation frame. The running example is a Nat block with add and double:
section.code: (add-Z) ⟨Zero | add(n; α)⟩ ⇝ ⟨n | α⟩ (add-S) ⟨Succ(m) | add(n; α)⟩ ⇝ ⟨m | add(n; Succ⁻(α))⟩ (dbl-Z) ⟨Zero | double(α)⟩ ⇝ ⟨Zero | α⟩ (dbl-S) ⟨Succ(m) | double(α)⟩ ⇝ ⟨m | double(Succ⁻(Succ⁻(α)))⟩
section.prose:
Here Succ⁻(α) := μ̃x.⟨Succ(x) | α⟩ is the return-side constructor frame — definable, not primitive. Elaborating recursion on the argument into an accumulator frame is the standard sequent-machine flattening
: no rule ever searches a term tree; every redex sits at the cut. The elaboration of the reserved rule faces into cells is built in theory-computads (its elaborate layer), the acceptance target that flips rule from parse-and-decline to accepted-behind-gate.

section.title: Critical pairs at the seam
section.prose: A pipeline add(double(x), n) focuses to ⟨x | double(add(n; α))⟩ — the consumer is a composition of frames. An overlap arises where one cell's right side materializes a pattern another cell's left side matches: (dbl-S) produces Succ⁻ frames that feed add's left side one constructor at a time. The composite worth fusing is the frame pair Succ⁻(add(n; α)), whose one-step behavior is derivable:
section.code: ⟨v | Succ⁻(add(n; α))⟩ ≡ ⟨Succ(v) | add(n; α)⟩ ⇝ ⟨v | add(n; Succ⁻(α))⟩
section.prose:
Completion therefore synthesizes the consumer-level commutation cell (fuse-S⁻-add), Succ⁻(add(n; α)) ⇝ add(n; Succ⁻(α)), which eliminates the intermediate Succ allocation entirely — deforestation as a derived 2-cell, with the derivation above as its certificate. (A consumer cell K₁ ⇝ K₂ abbreviates the producer-quantified command cell ⟨v | K₁⟩ ⇝ ⟨v | K₂⟩; the engine stores the quantified form.) First-class consumers are what make the overlap syntactically visible — under CPS the same overlap hides behind a lambda. That the fused cell is the two-step composite of its parts is the concurrency-theorem reading, adopted as the differential contract
.

section.title: The engine: cell store, overlap enumeration, completion
section.prose:
The engine has four built parts. A cell store holds cells as content-addressed inspectable IR, pattern identity keyed on node hashes. Overlap enumeration returns, for each cell pair, the complete family of left-side unifications at a
— the multi-sum shape: every overlap, never a single chosen one. Cuts make overlaps shallow (the seam is the root), which is exactly why this is tractable where tree rewriting needs full subterm traversal
. The completion loop runs Knuth–Bendix / Squier completion over the convergent slice
: it normalizes both reducts of each critical pair, emits a tracelet (the 3-cell
) for a joinable pair, and turns a requested fusion shortcut into a derived cell whose certificate is the pair of joining paths. Termination is bounded by a completion budget with decline-and-report, the same posture as the machine step budget: exhausting the step or cell ceiling is a defined decline carrying the pending overlaps, never divergence or a panic.

Correctness is differential plus replay, not trust. Every derived cell is property-tested — applying the fused cell agrees with applying the constituent path over generated ground configurations, the concurrency theorem adopted as a test, its category-theoretic proof machinery explicitly not implemented — and every certificate is replayed, re-executing both paths and comparing, rather than trusted. Replay is promoted to the identity criterion: two tracelets are the same transformation when they replay equal (
), which is what makes tracelet grafting associative and unital in the formal reading.

Each cell carries derived — never user-declared — metadata: a per-metavariable
with a linearity flag, and an invertibility flag (true for completion-emitted joinability certificates, false for oriented optimization cells), computed at elaboration. That metadata is what the two-mode certificate composition reads — an unconditional coherence lane for invertible certificates, and a directed lane gated by variable-flow acyclicity across the composed seam that declines a cycle with the cycle as diagnostic. The metadata and the two composition modes are the VDC-reflection deltas to this engine; their formal reading is homed in the reflection-face component, and this engine is the cell store that face grounds.

section.title: Scope and honest limits
section.prose:
Three limits, stated honestly. Natives are opaque: a prim command reduces in Rust and has no seam a cell can see through, so every fusion claim is scoped to the cell-visible fragment — the symbolic command-pattern IL of datatype constructors, operations, and the two return-side frames — and re-expressing hot natives as cells is future work. Non-linear overlaps fan out: completion returns overlap-indexed families of composites, and a single canonical fused rule exists only on a linear seam. This fan-out is not a shortfall but the mathematically forced behavior — it is the virtual in the reflection face's virtual double category, where loose composites need not exist and, under duplication, exist only as the multi-sum-indexed family. Finally, the η discipline binds completion: a joining path may use codata-η only at a negative cut and data-η only at a positive cut, checked against the
of the seam — the strategy-tied η vocabulary is realized as the cell's η-kind.

section.title: Why completion beats pragmas, and the gate
section.prose:
Pragma systems bolt unverified, unoriented equations onto a fixed evaluator, out of band from the datatype. Here the cells are declared in the data block as siblings of constructors (the anti-retrofit guard), oriented by the same
discipline that runs the machine, completed into a convergent system with machine-checkable certificates, and differential-tested. The folklore that lazy languages get obvious fusions for free is explained rather than envied: call-by-name orientation makes the seam demand-transparent, and the polarized kernel gives both orientations locally, per type, instead of globally per language. The same localization move recurs across the design — where a global gluing property fails, localize the choice per cut and restrict the global operation — and the composition gate is its correctness side. The list combinators are the obvious first fusion targets; the engine's bridge reifies exactly that frozen fragment (the Nil / Cons / Pair correspondences) into the command arena.

The phase-L2 gate is the fused-equals-two-step differential over generated ground configurations, certificate replay, and the η-polarity pathological pins — an η-step at the wrong polarity must be rejected by the engine. A disagreement is a genuine defect in the matching, substitution, or splicing engine — a finding, never a tolerated divergence — the same posture as the L1 differential.

section.title: Closures as rewrites (the closures lane, design)
section.prose: Closure conversion is an in-IL rewrite, adopted at exactly one site — the U/force boundary (gandr's lambda is a computation and is never bound, so no lambda-site closures exist). An environment-carrying thunk captures part of the ambient context; the closure cell fires like any other seam rule, and a confluent CC rewrite drives every free variable into the explicit environment:
section.code: ς ::= ε | ς, v/x -- explicit environments (IL syntax) (βU) ⟨{ς, force → M} | force(K)⟩ ⇝ ⟨M[ς] | K⟩ -- the closure cell, a seam rule like any other (CC) {ς, force → M} ⇝ {(ς, x/x), force → M} -- for x ∈ FV(M) ∖ Dom(ς); oriented, confluent -- modulo environment reordering
section.prose:
CC-normal form — no free variable outside the environment — is the lowering gate: pre-lowering runs CC to normal form, and each closure lowers to a flat (env-struct, code-pointer) pair, the runtime closure shape the arena machine already builds. The adequacy result — a capturing machine agrees with a lookup-only machine on CC-normal programs — upgrades the jit-equals-eval correspondence from a test to a theorem on the closure fragment, with the differential retained regardless
. Grades refine capture (a grade-0 variable need not be captured at all), and environment sharing and lambda-lifting are derived cells in the same store, with environments hashconsed after CC-normalization so canonical minimal environments deduplicate. The proof-debt ledger is named, not hidden: confluence of CC is modulo environment reordering — the Agda face needs a permutation quotient to sit in the Squier-degenerate slice — and the source theory covers pure and call-by-need but not effects.

The effects-and-closure-conversion composite is staged, because the two literatures are disjoint: every closure-conversion correctness proof is pure or state-only, every handler-compilation result performs no closure conversion, so the intersection is empty and the composite is genuinely open. The staged posture states the closure equalities now on the pure and call-by-need fragment (Sullivan's backward simulation and Kripke-heap logical relation apply essentially verbatim); adopts capability / evidence-passing as the handler-elimination leg with citable correctness, modeling gandr's op-keyed deep handlers on multi-prompt delimited control rather than single-prompt shift/reset
; and names as staged proof debt the composite theorem — upgrading the Kripke-heap relation to a biorthogonal step-indexed logical relation for handlers over the sharing heap
, cohered against the confluent fine-grained handler reduction theory the completion engine's cells must respect
. No published work combines all three, so gandr's stage would be a first — recorded as debt, never claimed early; a fallback pure-lambda handler translation
and the nearest closure-conversion-under-effects result (state only)
bound the boundary, and the jit-equals-eval differential over effectful corpus programs covers the composite meanwhile.

This is design, not built. The closure producer is deliberately absent at L0 — the focusing translation emits the pre-closure-conversion codata form instead, and closure conversion lands later as an in-IL rewrite. The lane is also where a copattern / handler unification would eventually sit, since compositional copatterns and delimited control are one mechanism
.

section.title: Phases and gates
section.prose: The kernel lands in four gated phase gates , none touching the frozen core before the last. Each phase carries its own status below.

section.title: Phase L0 — the command IR and focusing
section.prose: The command IR, the focusing translation, a pretty-printer, and inspection hooks. Its gate: focusing is total on the corpus and the typed-IL debug assertions pass.

section.title: Phase L1 — the L machine and its differential
section.prose: The L machine: transitions, store, memo write-back, and a single step budget. Its gate was the differential L-run of the focused image agreeing with the driver on the full corpus plus property strategies. Through the migration the CEK machine was the external oracle: an independently-maintained implementation of the same operational semantics, so agreement was evidence for the L machine's correctness. The CEK retired at B1 stage F, so the L machine is now the sole driver; the differential's reference is the frozen outcome snapshots that captured the final oracle-agreeing run — the same canonicalization, its reference now a fixture rather than a live second machine — and the conformance soundness rows are re-anchored on L outcomes. L1 is partial: the readback residuals stay tracked (the un-focusing translation, prelude free-name resolution in force position, the whole-program identity-former decline, and the declared-data eliminator decline), each reporting a defined unsupported-by-reference outcome rather than a panic.

section.title: Phase L2 — the fusion engine
section.prose: The cell store, overlap enumeration at cut seams, Knuth–Bendix / Squier completion, replayable tracelet certificates, and the two-mode certificate composition, flipping rewrite rules from parse-and-decline to accepted-behind-gate. Its design is absorbed in the fusion section above and its engineering face is built in crate theory-computads; the phase-L2 gate — the fused-equals-two-step differential, certificate replay, and the η-polarity pathological pins — is realized as that crate's differential harness. The category-theoretic proof machinery of the concurrency theorem is explicitly not implemented; the differential is its witness.

section.title: Phase L3 — the promotion decision
section.prose:
The last phase is the promotion decision , an ADR either way and the only phase that may touch the frozen core. Position (a): L stays the runtime and optimization IL with the call-by-push-value core canonical — the Sequent Core position
. Position (b): command syntax enters the frozen core (an ADR plus a dictionary entry plus an Agda face, competing for the post-arena window with the data surface's nominal tag). The decision is explicit, evidence-based, and reversible until taken, gated on the evidence L1 and L2 accumulate plus the codata and lowering experience; until it is taken everything the kernel adds is additive, touching no frozen-core code. Its design is recorded here; the decision itself is deferred. The fusion engine already takes a related boundary — that its cells range over the symbolic
rather than the arena command IL directly — as a draft-ADR candidate rather than minting an ADR: if position (b) is chosen, the relationship between the two should be pinned by an ADR.
